name: {0} Fire Arrow
description: See Fire Arrows in the handbook.
guide-text:
Crafting
Fire arrows are independent items with tinder and rope models. Original arrow materials plus one rope and one dry grass make the corresponding fire arrow, retaining quantity and trait requirements. Any supported ordinary arrow can also be wrapped directly: 1 arrow + 1 rope + 1 dry grass makes 1 fire arrow of the same material in any grid arrangement.

Use
Hold a lit torch in the other hand for one second. Nearby fires also ignite fresh arrows, including in flight. Bows prioritize burning arrows. Original damage and break chance are retained. Rope arrows have no fire variant.

Environment
Default fuel budget: 300 seconds. Regional dampness reduces this to roughly 244-300 seconds in calm, rain-free weather. Strong wind, rain exposure and extreme dampness can extinguish flames. Dampness is estimated from regional rainfall and current weather, not relative humidity. Roofs block rain; snow is not rain. Relative airflow and water are checked during flight.

Impact and recovery
Placed wood furniture and other flammable materials can catch fire. Clutter without material declarations uses its predominant model surface material. Flight segments detect collisionless grass and plants; solid walls block ignition. Claims and reinforcement-breaking privileges are respected. Each burning arrow removes 10 reinforcement from each contacted block only once, including across chunk reloads. Positive strength prevents ignition; flammable blocks can ignite on the hit that exhausts it. Zero-strength lock records do not prevent burning. Stone remains inert even after losing reinforcement. Fresh and extinguished arrows cannot damage reinforcement. Inert surfaces extinguish arrows in about four seconds or less. Surviving arrows can be recovered. Names distinguish fuel exhaustion, water, wind, rain, dampness and surface contact. Extinguished arrows lose the tinder and binding, have charred heads in inventory, hands, on the ground and in flight, and cannot relight but remain usable ammunition. Arrows of the same material and state stack to 64; different extinguishing causes remain separate. Merging lit arrows keeps the shorter remaining lifetime and never restores fuel. Storage and restarts do not reset the burning deadline.
